BiblicalUsage: These palm-shaped carvings dressed the temple Solomon built. The walls were carved round about with cherubims and palm trees and open flowers, and the greater house was cieled with fir, overlaid with gold, and set with palm trees and chains.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the carving says something plain about worship: God's house was made beautiful on purpose, with the living shapes of His creation cut into its walls.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
